title: Representing booleans
context: How is a boolean represented in MySQL?

source.title: JavaGuide (Snailclimb): MySQL questions
source.note: Question and topic from this JavaGuide article. The answer is an original English write-up; see content/sources/javaguide/NOTICE.md.

answer: MySQL has no native boolean. `BOOLEAN` is an alias for `TINYINT(1)`, where 0 is false and any non-zero value is true. Reads may return 0 or 1, and drivers map them to booleans. For clarity in a schema, many teams use `TINYINT(1)` or `BIT(1)` and document the meaning. Prefer a `NOT NULL` constraint so the value is always 0 or 1.

points.title: BOOLEAN is TINYINT(1)
points.why: The stored value is a small integer, not a true boolean type.

points.title: Use NOT NULL
points.why: Without NOT NULL, a third state, NULL, appears and breaks simple checks.
